handover.text: Bed one: Rohit Kulkarni, day one after his appendix. His mother hasn't left that chair since.
Bed five: Mrs. Banerjee, seventy-seven, pneumonia. Coughs like a tractor and calls everyone 'beta'.
Three, four and six are sleeping off their operations. And Emergency is sending us a new one.
This week you're on the ward, {called}. Rounds, admissions, families. Wednesday night you're on call.
And a warning. Every bed on this ward is full, and Mr. Malhotra counts beds the way misers count coins.

choose.text: Ready. Where do I start?

then.text: Where every round starts. With the patient you know.

choose.text: Honestly? I'm more scared of the families than the surgery.

then.text: Good. The ones who aren't scared of families don't last.
then.head: nod

then.text: Start with the patient you know. Bed one.

choose.text: Who is Mr. Malhotra?

then.text: The administrator. Excel sheets for blood. You'll meet him. Everybody does.
Bed one first. Go.
Doctor. They brought him back from intensive care at six. He's so pale.
Mum. I'm fine. I'm... mostly fine.
then.head: down

then.text: The infection spread before we got there. The antibiotics are working now. Slowly.
Doctor! They let me have tea. Hospital tea. It's terrible. I love it.
He was in recovery for hours. Hours! Nobody told me anything.
There was some bleeding. It's stopped. He's doing well.

else.text: Doctor! I walked to the toilet. By myself. Nobody clapped.
He ate two idlis. Two! Yesterday he couldn't drink water.

rohit_round.text: So. My exams are on Thursday. I can go, right?
Say yes. Please. He's worked three years for this.

choose.text: Not Thursday. Your wound needs a week before you sit in an exam hall for three hours.

then.text: A week? But...
then.head: down

then.text: Your college will give you a medical certificate. We write very convincing ones.
...Okay. Okay. At least I get to revise in bed.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Let's see how you are on Wednesday. If you're walking well, we'll talk.

then.text: Careful, {called}. Hope is a promise to a mother.
Wednesday. I'm holding you to it, Doctor.

choose.text: If it means that much, go. Just take the painkillers.

then.text: No. He'll split his wound open on a bench. Thursday is a no.
Don't promise what the body can't keep, {called}.
Right. Sorry. I knew it, really.
then.head: down

rohit_round.text: Good. Now: Emergency's patient is in the admissions bay.

lakshmi_arrive.text: Lakshmi Pillai, fifty-eight. Pain under the ribs since last night. Vomited twice.
It comes like a wave. Then it squeezes. Then it goes. Then it comes back.
Doctor, I have a pressure cooker on at home. Can this be quick?

choose.text: We'll be thorough first, quick second. Your neighbour can turn off the cooker.

then.text: Hmph. Thorough. Fine. Ask.
then.head: nod

choose.text: The faster you answer, the faster this goes.

then.text: My son talks to me like that. Ask, then.

lakshmi_arrive.text: History first, then examine her. Questions are limited, {called}. So is her patience.

then.text: Gallbladder. Inflamed, infected. Antibiotics today, and she's on my list tomorrow.

else.text: Look again at what you found. Pain under the right ribs, a fever, and she stopped mid-breath. Gallbladder.

then.text: And you found the metformin. We stop it before surgery and watch her sugar.
then.head: nod

else.text: Doctor? Her bag. Metformin tablets. She's diabetic. Nobody asked her.
Medicines, {called}. Always medicines.

lakshmi_after.text: Surgery? I said quick, not surgery!
My son is going to call. He'll want to know everything. Everything.
lakshmi_after.head: down

lakshmi_after.text: We'll move you to bed two. It's by the window.

arjun_call.text: Hello? Hello? Mummy, turn the phone. I can see the ceiling. Is that the doctor?
Doctor, I want the truth. Is it cancer? Why does she need surgery? Is it because of her sugar?
Doctor... I never told him about the sugar. Please.
arjun_call.head: down

choose.text: Mrs. Pillai, may I tell Arjun about your diabetes? It's your choice.

then.text: ...Tell him. He'll shout. Then he'll calm down. Then he'll send mangoes.
then.head: nod

then.text: Arjun, your mother has diabetes. It's controlled with tablets. It isn't why she needs surgery, but we'll watch her sugar.
Mummy! Since when? ...Okay. Okay. Thank you for telling me straight, Doctor.

choose.text: Arjun, your mother can tell you what she wants you to know. It's gallstones, not cancer.

then.text: Can tell me? I'm her son! I pay for... fine. Gallstones. Fine.
Thank you, Doctor. I'll tell him myself. One day. Maybe tomorrow.

choose.text: She's diabetic, Arjun. On tablets. She should have told you.

then.text: DIABETIC? Mummy! Doctor, thank you. At least someone tells me things.
That was mine to tell, Doctor. Mine.

arjun_call.text: Doctor, I'm getting on a plane. Thursday. Look after her.

malhotra_beds.text: Ah. {called}. Vikram Malhotra, administration. Walk with me. No, stand. Faster.
Ward 4 is at a hundred and four percent. Emergency has six on trolleys. I need two beds by noon.
Bed one: the appendix boy. He's walking, he's eating, send him home.
Bed two: the gallstones lady. Tablets, home, back in six weeks for her operation. Everybody wins.
Rohit is one day after surgery, Mr. Malhotra.
Sister, the doctor can speak. {called}? Two beds. Yes?

choose.text: Let me check each of them properly. If it's safe for them to go, they go.

then.text: Rohit can go tomorrow if he eats lunch. Mrs. Pillai has a fever. She stays.
One bed. Tomorrow. ...You're going to be expensive, {called}.

choose.text: No. Neither of them is safe to send home today.

then.text: Not safe. Everybody says not safe. Emergency also is not safe, Doctor, with six on trolleys.
I'll remember this conversation.

choose.text: Fine. Two beds. They can both go home.

then.text: Finally. A doctor who understands arithmetic.
{called}. She has a fever.
then.head: shake

then.text: We'll talk about this.

malhotra_beds.text: Good. Good. I have a board meeting about the side room. Private rooms pay, Doctor. Remember that.

then.text: Mrs. Pillai came back at three this morning. Fever of thirty-nine, yellow as a turmeric root.
Sent home with tablets, back in an ambulance. She's on my list as an emergency now.

choose.text: That was my call. I was wrong, and I'm sorry.

then.text: Good. Say it to her too. Then never send a fever home again.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Mr. Malhotra needed the beds. Emergency was full.

then.text: Mr. Malhotra doesn't hold the pen. You do.

else.text: Mrs. Pillai's on my list at ten. Gallbladder out, sugar watched. You did that well.

then.text: And Rohit ate all his lunch yesterday. He's going home this morning. He asked for you.

day5_morning.text: Admissions again. A young man. He arrived with a phone in one hand and an uncle in the other.
Treat the wrist, {called}. Not the uncle.

kunal_arrive.text: Finally! Do you know how long I've been on this trolley? Forty minutes. I'm live-streaming it.
Kunal Bhatia, twenty-four. Fell off his scooter outside a club at six this morning.
My uncle is the health minister's... well. He knows the health minister. Private room. Now.

choose.text: Let's see the wrist first. Rooms come later.

then.text: Fine. Look. But gently. I play the guitar.
then.head: tilt

choose.text: Everyone on this ward gets the same care, Mr. Bhatia. Including you.

then.text: Wow. Did you get that, everyone? 'The same care'. Wow.
Good news, Mr. Bhatia. It's a sprain. A splint, ice, painkillers. You can go home today.

else.text: It needs a proper look in the fracture clinic. For now: a splint, ice and painkillers.

kunal_room.text: Home? My uncle said I'd get the side room. With a TV.
{called}! The chairman called. Mr. Bhatia's uncle called the chairman. The side room. Today.
The side room is for Mrs. Banerjee. Her pneumonia could spread through the whole ward.
Mrs. Banerjee has coughed in that bed for a week. One more day won't hurt.

choose.text: It's a sprain. He needs a splint and a taxi, not a bed. Mrs. Banerjee gets the side room.

then.text: You'll regret this. One-star review. One star!
The chairman will call me. And I will call you, {called}.

choose.text: Mrs. Banerjee gets the side room. Mr. Bhatia can have her bed overnight, for observation.

then.text: A ward bed. Next to strangers. Fine. One night.
Observation. Hm. I can sell that to the chairman.

choose.text: Fine. Mr. Bhatia has the side room.

then.text: Was that so hard? You've been very helpful. Follow me on Instagram.
...I'll tell Mrs. Banerjee to cough quietly.
then.head: shake

aarav_arrive.text: Doctor! We met on your first day, remember? He swallowed something. Again.
It was shiny. It was a secret.
aarav_arrive.head: tilt

aarav_arrive.text: The TV remote is open on the floor. Or it was a coin from my purse. I don't know!
Here's his film. Something round in his gullet. Read it, {called}. Properly.

choose.text: Aarav, was it a round shiny thing? Like a little silver button?

then.text: ...Maybe. Am I in trouble?
then.head: down

then.text: No. But your gullet might be. Let's look.

choose.text: Let me look at the film.

then.text: Please hurry.
then.head: down

then.text: A button battery. Two hours and it burns through his gullet. Good reading. I'll call the scope team.

else.text: Look at the edge again. Two rings: a halo. And the step from the side. It's a battery.
A coin can wait. A battery burns. Never guess with a child's gullet.

aarav_after.text: A battery? From the remote? Oh God. Aarav!
Can I have it back after?
aarav_after.head: tilt

choose.text: We'll take it out, Aarav. You'll be asleep. And no, you can't have it back.

then.text: Can I keep the X-ray?
Thank you, Doctor. Thank you. Again.

choose.text: Mrs. Thomas, he needs it out within the hour. The team will take him now.

then.text: Now. Yes. Okay. Aarav, hold my hand.
then.head: nod

night_start.text: So you're my intern tonight. Kabir Sethi. Senior resident. Nine years of nights.
Two rules. Call me if someone is dying. Don't call me if they're not.
I'm in the doctors' room. I'll be asleep. I'll forgive you exactly once.

choose.text: I'd rather call too early than too late.

then.text: ...Right answer. Annoying, but right.
then.head: nod

choose.text: I'll manage. Get some sleep.

then.text: That's what the last intern said. Call me early.

night_start.text: Mrs. Banerjee is awake again. She won't settle until a doctor sees her.

banerjee_night.text: Beta. You came. I can't sleep. Every time I close my eyes I cough.

then.text: And that boy in the glass room has his music on. All night. Thump, thump.
This little room is so quiet. Somebody fought for it, Sister says.
then.head: tilt

then.text: This little room is so quiet. Somebody fought for it, Sister says.
then.head: tilt

banerjee_night.text: My husband was a ship's radio officer. Forty years he listened to the sea at night. Now I listen for him.
banerjee_night.head: down

choose.text: Can I sit with you for a minute?

then.text: Tell me something. Anything. Tell me why you became a doctor.
then.head: tilt

then.text: Because someone held my grandfather's hand once, at night, and he said it was the best thing anyone did for him.
Then hold mine. ...There. Now I'll sleep.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Let me check your oxygen, and I'll ask Priya for something for the cough.

then.text: Ninety-four. Not bad for an old engine. Thank you, beta.
then.head: nod

rider_arrive.text: Motorbike. No helmet. A passer-by brought him in and left. No wallet, no name.
His pressure's falling. Where do you want me?

rider_after.text: Theatre's free. Blood bank wants a signature. And... your phone, Doctor. Administration.
{called}. Sorry, the night porter woke me. I hear we have an unidentified patient.
No ID. No insurance. No deposit. The policy is clear: stabilise and transfer to the government hospital.

choose.text: He's bleeding from an artery. He goes to theatre now. We can argue about money when he's alive.

then.text: This is not your decision to make at two in the morning, Doctor.
It's exactly my decision at two in the morning. Goodnight, Mr. Malhotra.
...I'll tell theatre.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Let me call Dr. Sethi. He'll decide with me.

then.text: I heard 'artery'. Theatre. Now. Mr. Malhotra, send me the bill. Personally.
...Fine. Fine! Theatre.
Good call, calling. I'll scrub. You keep pressing.
then.head: nod

choose.text: I'll keep pressure on and arrange the transfer.

then.text: Doctor, he won't survive the ambulance.
Who is transferring a bleeding artery? Nobody. Theatre, now. We'll talk later, {called}.

rider_after.text: His phone again. It says Pooja. It's been ringing for an hour.

choose.text: I'll answer it.

then.text: Papa? Papa, where are you? You said you'd bring a cake.
Hello. I'm a doctor at the hospital. Your papa had an accident on his bike. He's alive, and we're looking after him.
...Is he hurt? It's my birthday. He promised.
He's hurt, but he's in the best place. What's his name, sweetheart? And can a grown-up come?
Salim Sheikh. Salim. Mummy's coming. Tell Papa it's okay about the cake.

choose.text: Let it ring. Theatre first.

then.text: I'll answer it. Someone should.
then.head: nod

then.text: His name's Salim Sheikh. His daughter. His wife's on her way.

day7_morning.text: Kabir told me about your night.

then.text: A bleeding artery and you reached for the transfer form. He nearly died in our lift.
Policies are written in daylight by people who never see the patient. You see the patient.
You called your senior when it mattered. Kabir says that's rarer than it should be.
then.head: nod

else.text: Straight to theatre, and you told Mr. Malhotra goodnight. He told the whole board.
Half of them were horrified. The other half bought you a samosa. It's on the desk.

day7_morning.text: Today, Dr. Rao does his round. Head of Surgery. And Mr. Fernandes in bed six came in overnight.
His children are with him. Both of them. Shouting in whispers.

salim_morning.text: You're the night doctor? Pooja said a doctor talked to her. A kind one.
salim_morning.head: tilt

salim_morning.text: Fourteen orders a day, Doctor. Rain or sun. Last night a car came round the corner. Then nothing.
salim_morning.head: down

salim_morning.text: Who pays for all this? I have twelve hundred rupees in the bank.

choose.text: The social worker will help with the bills. Your job is to get better.

then.text: And my bike? No, don't answer. The bike is a problem for a man who can stand.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Today you owe Pooja a birthday cake. Everything else can wait.

then.text: A cake. Yes. Chocolate. She'll forgive me for chocolate.

joseph_arrive.text: Doctor! Finally. Papa's been vomiting all night. Green. Do something.
Maria, let the doctor breathe. And let Papa breathe.
My children. Thirty years they've argued about who loves me more. Neither of them asks me anything.
joseph_arrive.head: tilt

then.text: Adhesions. The old scar's bands have kinked his bowel. Often a tube and a drip let it settle.

else.text: His old scar, the tinkling, no hernia. It's adhesions: bands from his old surgery.

joseph_family.text: Then operate! Today! Do everything. He's my father.
He's eighty-one. No more cutting. Take the tubes out and let him go home to his garden.

choose.text: Mr. Fernandes. What would you like?

then.text: I want to see my granddaughter married in December. If a tube in my nose gets me there, a tube it is.
And if it needs the knife, I'll take the knife. But not today, and not because anybody shouted.
Then we start with a tube and a drip. If it hasn't settled in two days, we talk about surgery. All of us.
...Okay. Okay, Papa.
then.head: nod

then.text: Thank you, Doctor. For asking him. We forgot to.
then.head: down

choose.text: Maria's right. We should operate today.

then.text: Not first. Adhesions often settle without the knife, and he's eighty-one. Tube and drip first.
Nobody asked me. Again.
then.head: down

choose.text: Peter has a point. He could go home and rest.

then.text: A blocked bowel at home is a death sentence. He stays, with a tube and a drip.
Nobody asked me. Again.
then.head: down

rao_round.text: Ah. The famous intern. Anand Rao. I've heard about your week from three directions.
Dr. Rao, the board meets on Monday. Ward 4 runs over a hundred percent. Four general beds become two private rooms. It pays for the ward.
And the patients in those four beds?
Go elsewhere. Or go home sooner. Efficiency.
{called}. You've been on this ward all week. What did you see?

choose.text: I saw what going home sooner costs.

then.text: I sent Mrs. Pillai home with a fever to free a bed. She came back at three in the morning in an ambulance. That was my mistake, and a bed was why.

else.text: Mrs. Pillai had a fever. Sent home, she'd have come back at night in an ambulance. Keeping her one day saved a week.

then.text: And we put a sprained wrist in the side room while a woman with pneumonia coughed on five other patients.

else.text: And the side room went to the patient with pneumonia, not the one with an uncle. Nobody else caught it.

then.text: And a man nearly bled to death while I filled in a transfer form. I won't do that again.

else.text: And a delivery rider with no ID is alive because we didn't wait for a deposit.

then.text: Mr. Malhotra. Write that in your spreadsheet.
then.head: nod

then.text: ...Two more weeks. Then I want numbers. Real numbers, Doctor.

choose.text: I'm an intern. I think that's above me.

then.text: Nothing on my ward is above the people who work on it. Think about that.
Very sensible. Monday, then, Dr. Rao.

choose.text: The hospital has to pay its bills. Private rooms keep the lights on.

then.text: Finally, someone who reads the accounts!
Lights on and nobody in the beds. Hm.
then.head: shake

rao_round.text: Tomorrow, {called}. Your review. Don't be late.

letters.text: Post for you, {called}. A week on the ward and already you get post.

then.text: From Rohit. 'Thank you for not giving up on me. I'm writing my exams next month. Dr. Iyer says I can.'

else.text: From Rohit. A drawing of you as a superhero. The cape says 'APPENDIX'.

then.text: Mrs. Pillai asked for a different doctor for her follow-up. That's a letter too, of a kind.
then.head: shake

else.text: Mrs. Pillai. 'My son sent mangoes. Some are for you. Do not tell him I said so.'

then.text: And this is from Aarav. It's a robot. It's you. The robot is holding a battery.

else.text: And this is from Aarav. It's a robot. It has a very big X-ray.

then.text: And this one came with a slice of birthday cake. 'Thank you for answering the phone. From Pooja, age 9.'

else.text: And Salim's wife left sweets for the night staff. You're the night staff.

then.text: Mr. Fernandes's tube came out this morning. Settled, no surgery. He says you're invited to a wedding.

letters.text: Go on. Dr. Rao is waiting. Shoulders back.

review.text: Sit, {called}. Or stand. This isn't a trial. Or it is, but a short one.

then.text: Told a nineteen-year-old he couldn't sit his exams, and made him laugh about it. That's harder than an appendix.

else.text: Rohit's mother still asks for {called} by name. That's worth more than my report.

then.text: Found a sick gallbladder under a pressure cooker and a son in Dubai.
then.head: nod

then.text: Sent home a fever under pressure. Owned it the next morning. Hasn't done it since.
Reached for a form when a man was bleeding. Learnt from it, I think. I hope.
then.head: tilt

then.text: Called me when it mattered. Woke me exactly once. I've forgiven it.

else.text: Took a bleeding artery to theatre and told the administrator goodnight. I'd have done the same. Louder.

then.text: And Mrs. Banerjee slept, for the first time in a week, because someone held her hand.
then.head: nod

then.text: You told Mr. Malhotra the truth in front of me. Ward 4 keeps its beds. Nobody's done that in years.

else.text: You kept quiet when the beds were on the table. Next time, the patients need your voice.

review.text: You're not finished, {called}. Nobody is, after one week. But you listen, and you learn faster than you fall.
From Monday: Junior Resident. Congratulations, Doctor.

choose.text: Thank you. All of you. I couldn't have done it without you.

then.text: No. You couldn't. Remember that when you've got interns of your own.
then.head: nod

choose.text: Thank you. I'm ready for more.

then.text: Good. More is coming. Theatre lists, Monday. Bring that confidence and a spare pair of socks.

choose.text: I made mistakes this week.

then.text: Everyone does. The good ones remember them.
then.head: nod

review.text: Junior Resident. Which means more nights. Welcome.

quiet_morning.text: Morning, {called}. Quiet day. Don't say the word 'quiet' out loud, it's bad luck.
Theatre lists start soon. Until then, teaching films at the lightbox. Sharp eyes save lives.

then.text: A coin. You looked before you leapt. Good.
then.head: nod

else.text: A coin, {called}. Look before you call the scope team at midnight.

quiet_after.text: That's enough for today. Go home. Sleep. It's allowed.
